audit.why: Mel bullies melee Ekko pre-6; Chronobreak flips the lane and his roam tempo keeps it flipped (46.87% WR, TRICKY tag).

audit.whatIsWrong: Content chart off by one: whys[4] (Level 6 row) says 'At 5 he still has no Chronobreak' and win[4]='Mel' while full phases[4].side='Ekko' and the page's own spikes[1]/late say 6 flips the lane.
audit.why: Chronobreak at 6 is Ekko's dive-with-insurance window; the two layers disagreed on the row.
audit.corrected: win[4] flipped to Ekko with a level-6 why; whys[5]/[6] rewritten to their actual stages; full sides aligned.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four applicable interactions were absent: Chronobreak makes him untargetable through your execute and heals him (anti-heal matters); Parallel Convergence shields his all-in; Phase Dive is an auto-reset whose wind-up is the step-back tell.
audit.why: All four are in the kit flags/text and none reached the page.
audit.corrected: Folded into breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[2].d, report[5].t and report[8].t.

audit.why: R 110/80/50, W 22s, E 9s from the kit.

audit.corrected: Both rewritten to match their titles.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Ekko Chronobreak: 110s at rank 1, 50 at rank 3 — he's untargetable during it and heals on arrival, so save your execute for after it. - Parallel Convergence is 22s: once the stun circle is spent, his all-in has no lock. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Melee Ekko must walk through the glow to trade — hold ground with W up and his third-hit passive never gets to stack on you.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: His Q Timewinder reflects; Phase Dive and Chronobreak do not — and the W anomaly shields him and stuns you if you stand inside it.

edits.before: Track Ekko’s Chronobreak: Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Ekko’s Chronobreak: erases your kill and bursts back — save damage for after it. His combo opens with Phase Dive's auto-reset wind-up: that's your step-back cue.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Luden's into Sorcerer's, then Shadowflame and Rabadon's. Zhonya's vs the divers your W can't answer.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Luden's into Sorcerer's, then Shadowflame and Rabadon's. Add anti-heal — Chronobreak heals him on return.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Q-volley the last-hit, bank Overwhelm, and keep W glowing — his Q Timewinder returns to him, so the reflect taxes both hits.

notes: Same off-by-one content chart as the diana matchup (whys written one stage early); packet chart's Mel-at-6 disagrees with the page's own 'Chronobreak changes everything' prose and the full layer's Ekko row, and the packet carries a flagged chart defect, so the kit-grounded 6-flip won. Ekko's W carries a projectile flag in the kit but its description is a placed anomaly, not a missile — did not claim it reflectable. Ratings untouched (rating scales with the named side per phases[4] 'Ekko 7/10'). report edits: two rewrites (report[5] folds the Phase Dive auto-reset tell, report[8] the Chronobreak anti-heal).
